answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
